## Account selection

When a user has multiple connected accounts for the same toolkit, specify which one the session uses:

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript', 'API']} persist>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
session = composio.sessions.create(
    user_id="user_123",
    connected_accounts={
        "gmail": ["ca_work_gmail"],
        "github": ["ca_personal_github"],
    }
)
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
import { Composio } from '@composio/core';
const composio = new Composio({ apiKey: 'your_api_key' });
// ---cut---
const session = await composio.create("user_123", {
  connectedAccounts: {
    gmail: ["ca_work_gmail"],
    github: ["ca_personal_github"],
  },
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="API">
```bash
curl -X POST https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/tool_router/session \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "user_id": "user_123",
    "connected_accounts": {"gmail": ["ca_work_gmail"], "github": ["ca_personal_github"]}
  }'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

<Callout type="info">
Arrays are the preferred format for `connectedAccounts`. A single string (e.g. `"ca_work_gmail"`) is still accepted for backwards compatibility and is automatically coerced to a single-element array. Only one account per toolkit is allowed when [multi-account mode](/docs/authentication/managing-multiple-connected-accounts) is disabled.
</Callout>

### Precedence

When executing a tool, the session selects the connected account in this order:

1. The `connectedAccounts` override, if provided in the session config.
2. The `authConfigs` override, which finds or creates a connection on that config.
3. An auth config previously created for this toolkit.
4. A new auth config created using Composio managed auth.
5. Otherwise, an error if no Composio managed auth scheme exists for the toolkit.

When a user has multiple connected accounts for a toolkit, the session uses the most recently connected one.

## Disabling the sandbox

By default, sessions include the [sandbox](/docs/sandbox/remote), a persistent environment that provides `COMPOSIO_REMOTE_WORKBENCH` and `COMPOSIO_REMOTE_BASH_TOOL`. If your use case doesn't need code execution, disable it:

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript', 'API']} persist>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
session = composio.sessions.create(
    user_id="user_123",
    sandbox={
        "enable": False
    }
)
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
// @noErrors
import { Composio } from '@composio/core';
const composio = new Composio({ apiKey: 'your_api_key' });
// ---cut---
const session = await composio.create("user_123", {
  sandbox: {
    enable: false,
  },
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="API">
```bash
# The REST API names the sandbox block `workbench`
curl -X POST https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/tool_router/session \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"user_id": "user_123", "workbench": {"enable": false}}'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

When disabled:
- `COMPOSIO_REMOTE_WORKBENCH` and `COMPOSIO_REMOTE_BASH_TOOL` are excluded from the session
- Sandbox-related system prompt lines are stripped
- Direct sandbox calls are rejected with a 400 error

[Zero Data Retention](/docs/security/zero-data-retention) does not cover the sandbox, so disable it in sessions that handle data that needs ZDR.

To keep the sandbox but block raw HTTP calls from it, set `enable_proxy_execution` (Python) or `enableProxyExecution` (TypeScript) to `false`. See [Proxy execute](/docs/extending-sessions/proxy-execute#session-restrictions) for how session restrictions apply to proxy calls.

<Callout>
`sandbox` is the preferred config key. `workbench` still works as a fully supported alias and isn't deprecated, so existing code keeps running unchanged.
</Callout>

## Sandbox compute tier

The sandbox runs per session. Pick a compute tier to match the workload: heavier code execution or larger in-memory data benefits from a bigger sandbox. Pass the tier via `sandbox.sandbox_size` (snake_case on the wire, `sandboxSize` in the TypeScript SDK).

<Callout type="info">
Requires `@composio/core` ≥ `0.8.1` (TypeScript) or `composio` ≥ `0.12.1` (Python). Older SDKs reject `sandboxSize` (TypeScript) or silently drop `sandbox_size` (Python). See the [release notes](/docs/changelog/2026/04/28).
</Callout>


| Tier       | vCPU | RAM   |
| ---------- | ---- | ----- |
| `standard` | 1    | 1 GB  |
| `medium`   | 2    | 2 GB  |
| `large`    | 4    | 4 GB  |
| `xlarge`   | 8    | 8 GB  |

Defaults to `standard` when omitted.

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript', 'API']} persist>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
session = composio.sessions.create(
    user_id="user_123",
    sandbox={
        "enable": True,
        "sandbox_size": "large",
    },
)
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
// @noErrors
import { Composio } from '@composio/core';
const composio = new Composio({ apiKey: 'your_api_key' });
// ---cut---
const session = await composio.create("user_123", {
  sandbox: {
    enable: true,
    sandboxSize: "large",
  },
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="API">
```bash
curl -X POST https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/tool_router/session \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"user_id": "user_123", "workbench": {"enable": true, "sandbox_size": "large"}}'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

<Callout type="info">
**Pricing:** Sandboxes are not billed today. Composio plans to begin billing for sandbox usage soon (metered by tier and runtime). Pick a tier that matches your workload, but expect future pricing to track actual usage.
</Callout>

Changing `sandbox_size` on an existing session recreates the sandbox on the next access. The sandbox's in-memory filesystem state is lost, but the persistent [`/mnt/files/` mount](/docs/sandbox/remote#files-and-mounts) survives the restart.

## Updating a session

`session.update()` patches the stored configuration in place. Fields you omit are preserved, so you can widen or narrow one part of a session without restating the rest. The SDK refreshes `session.config` and the session's config version only after the API accepts the change.

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript', 'API']} persist>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
session = composio.sessions.use("session_id")

session.update(toolkits={"enable": ["gmail", "github"]})
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
import { Composio } from '@composio/core';
const composio = new Composio({ apiKey: 'your_api_key' });
// ---cut---
const session = await composio.sessions.use("session_id");

await session.update({ toolkits: { enable: ["gmail", "github"] } });
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="API">
```bash
curl -X PATCH https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/tool_router/session/$SESSION_ID \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"toolkits": {"enable": ["gmail", "github"]}}'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

<Callout type="info">
The update behavior below requires `@composio/core` ≥ `0.19.1` (TypeScript) or `composio` ≥ `0.22.1` (Python).
</Callout>

### Maps replace, they don't merge

A `tools`, `authConfigs`, or `connectedAccounts` map you send replaces the stored map entirely. The API does not merge entries, so a Slack-only `tools` map removes a Gmail entry that was stored before it.

Stored before the update:

```json
{
  "tools": {
    "gmail": { "enable": ["GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS"] },
    "slack": { "enable": ["SLACK_SEND_MESSAGE"] }
  }
}
```

The update:

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript', 'API']} persist>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
session.update(
    tools={"slack": {"enable": ["SLACK_SEND_MESSAGE", "SLACK_LIST_CHANNELS"]}},
)
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
import { Composio } from '@composio/core';
const composio = new Composio({ apiKey: 'your_api_key' });
const session = await composio.sessions.use("session_id");
// ---cut---
await session.update({
  tools: { slack: { enable: ["SLACK_SEND_MESSAGE", "SLACK_LIST_CHANNELS"] } },
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="API">
```bash
curl -X PATCH https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/tool_router/session/$SESSION_ID \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"tools": {"slack": {"enable": ["SLACK_SEND_MESSAGE", "SLACK_LIST_CHANNELS"]}}}'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Stored after the update. The `gmail` entry is gone:

```json
{
  "tools": {
    "slack": { "enable": ["SLACK_SEND_MESSAGE", "SLACK_LIST_CHANNELS"] }
  }
}
```

To change one entry, send the whole map with every entry you want to keep. An empty map (`{}`) is stored as an explicit empty map.

The same rule applies to `toolkits`, `tags`, and `preload`: a value replaces the stored policy. `manageConnections`, `sandbox`, and `multiAccount` merge the subfields you send, and an empty object changes nothing.

### Narrowing an existing session to no app toolkits

An empty allowlist on update denies every app toolkit, exactly as it does on create. The SDK sends `{ "enable": [] }` as-is instead of dropping it from the request.

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript', 'API']} persist>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
session.update(toolkits={"enable": []})
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
import { Composio } from '@composio/core';
const composio = new Composio({ apiKey: 'your_api_key' });
const session = await composio.sessions.use("session_id");
// ---cut---
await session.update({ toolkits: { enable: [] } });
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="API">
```bash
curl -X PATCH https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/tool_router/session/$SESSION_ID \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"toolkits": {"enable": []}}'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

### Removing a callback URL

`manageConnections.callbackUrl: null` removes only the stored callback URL. `enable` and the other connection settings stay as they are. An empty string is rejected.

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript', 'API']} persist>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
session.update(manage_connections={"callback_url": None})
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
// @noErrors
import { Composio } from '@composio/core';
const composio = new Composio({ apiKey: 'your_api_key' });
const session = await composio.sessions.use("session_id");
// ---cut---
await session.update({ manageConnections: { callbackUrl: null } });
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="API">
{/* code-example: unchecked-api rule="api-body-schema" operation="PATCH /api/v3.1/tool_router/session/{session_id}" field="manage_connections.callback_url" reason="openapi.json types callback_url as a string; the API accepts null to remove it" */}
```bash
curl -X PATCH https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/tool_router/session/$SESSION_ID \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"manage_connections": {"callback_url": null}}'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

### Clearing a block with null

Passing `null` (`None` in Python) for a whole block removes the stored override and the session falls back to the default for that block. Every policy block accepts it: `toolkits`, `tools`, `tags`, `authConfigs`, `connectedAccounts`, `preload`, `manageConnections`, `sandbox`, `proxyExecute`, `multiAccount`, `search`, `execute`, and `experimental`.

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript', 'API']} persist>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
session.update(manage_connections=None, multi_account=None)
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
import { Composio } from '@composio/core';
const composio = new Composio({ apiKey: 'your_api_key' });
const session = await composio.sessions.use("session_id");
// ---cut---
await session.update({ manageConnections: null, multiAccount: null });
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="API">
```bash
curl -X PATCH https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/tool_router/session/$SESSION_ID \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"manage_connections": null, "multi_account": null}'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Clearing a policy can widen access. `toolkits: null` removes the toolkit policy and restores the unrestricted default, which is the opposite of `{ "enable": [] }`; clearing `preload` does the same for preloaded tools, so the agent can reach more than before the update. Send `toolkits: []` when you want to deny every app toolkit. Clearing `multiAccount` resolves to disabled, while omitting it preserves the stored setting.

### Blocks you can set only on update

`search`, `execute`, and `experimental` are not part of `create()`. Reach them with `session.update()` on an existing session.

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript', 'API']} persist>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
session.update(
    search={"enable": False},
    execute={"enable_multi_execute": False},
)
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
// @noErrors
import { Composio } from '@composio/core';
const composio = new Composio({ apiKey: 'your_api_key' });
const session = await composio.sessions.use("session_id");
// ---cut---
await session.update({
  search: { enable: false },
  execute: { enableMultiExecute: false },
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="API">
```bash
curl -X PATCH https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/tool_router/session/$SESSION_ID \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"search": {"enable": false}, "execute": {"enable_multi_execute": false}}'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Both blocks are on by default. `search` controls the session's search helper, so disabling it leaves the agent with the tools you preloaded. `execute.enableMultiExecute` controls whether the agent can run several tool calls in one request. `manageConnections.enableConnectionRemoval` is update-only as well, and controls whether the session exposes the connection-removal tool.

The `experimental` block on update holds server-side session settings: `permissions`, `linkUrlOverwrite`, `fastMode`, `submitFeedback`, and `sessionConfigId`. `sessionConfigId` applies a [saved Session config](/docs/session-configs#applying-a-config-to-an-existing-session) and can't be combined with `toolkits`, `tools`, or `tags`. The `experimental` block on update is a different field from the `experimental` option on `create()`, which holds [local tools and toolkits](/docs/extending-sessions/local-tools-and-toolkits) that run in your process, so `experimental: null` on an update leaves those alone.

### Multi-account mode after an update

The canonical disabled state is `{ "enable": false, "require_explicit_selection": false }` with no maximum. Sending `enable: false` resets a stale maximum or selection setting, and reapplying that disabled configuration is accepted. Combining `enable: false` with `maxAccountsPerToolkit` or `requireExplicitSelection: true` is rejected with a `400`.

### Preload must stay inside the policy

An update that narrows `toolkits`, `tools`, or `tags` while leaving an explicitly preloaded tool outside the new policy is rejected with a `400`, and nothing changes. Fix `preload` in the same update:

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript', 'API']} persist>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
session.update(
    toolkits={"enable": ["slack"]},
    preload={"tools": ["SLACK_SEND_MESSAGE"]},
)
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
import { Composio } from '@composio/core';
const composio = new Composio({ apiKey: 'your_api_key' });
const session = await composio.sessions.use("session_id");
// ---cut---
await session.update({
  toolkits: { enable: ["slack"] },
  preload: { tools: ["SLACK_SEND_MESSAGE"] },
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="API">
```bash
curl -X PATCH https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/tool_router/session/$SESSION_ID \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"toolkits": {"enable": ["slack"]}, "preload": {"tools": ["SLACK_SEND_MESSAGE"]}}'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

### Concurrent updates

Every session response carries a config version (`session.configVersion` in TypeScript, `session.config_version` in Python, `config_version` on the wire). By default, `session.update()` sends no precondition, so the last writer wins. To make an update conditional, pass the version you read as `expectedConfigVersion` (`expected_config_version` in Python). The API then applies the update only when the stored version still matches. Otherwise it answers `409` and writes nothing: no config change, no history entry, no cache update. The SDK never retries that request, so a conflict is reported exactly once.

<Callout type="info">
The API must support `expected_config_version`. If it doesn't, it rejects a conditional update with a `400`.
</Callout>

On a conflict, the SDK raises `ComposioSessionConfigConflictError` (TypeScript) or `SessionConfigConflictError` (Python) and leaves the session object as it was. Re-read the session with `sessions.use()`, reapply your change on top of the fresh config, and retry:

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript', 'API']} persist>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
from composio.exceptions import SessionConfigConflictError

session = composio.sessions.use("session_id")

try:
    session.update(
        toolkits={"enable": ["gmail", "github"]},
        expected_config_version=session.config_version,
    )
except SessionConfigConflictError:
    # Another client changed the session first. Nothing was written.
    session = composio.sessions.use("session_id")
    session.update(
        toolkits={"enable": ["gmail", "github"]},
        expected_config_version=session.config_version,
    )
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
// @noErrors
import { Composio, ComposioSessionConfigConflictError } from '@composio/core';
const composio = new Composio({ apiKey: 'your_api_key' });
// ---cut---
let session = await composio.sessions.use("session_id");

try {
  await session.update({
    toolkits: { enable: ["gmail", "github"] },
    expectedConfigVersion: session.configVersion,
  });
} catch (error) {
  if (!(error instanceof ComposioSessionConfigConflictError)) throw error;
  // Another client changed the session first. Nothing was written.
  session = await composio.sessions.use("session_id");
  await session.update({
    toolkits: { enable: ["gmail", "github"] },
    expectedConfigVersion: session.configVersion,
  });
}
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="API">
{/* code-example: unchecked-api rule="api-body-schema" operation="PATCH /api/v3.1/tool_router/session/{session_id}" field="expected_config_version" reason="the PATCH endpoint accepts expected_config_version but its OpenAPI schema omits the field" */}
```bash
CONFIG_VERSION=$(curl -s -X GET https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/tool_router/session/$SESSION_ID \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" | jq -r '.config_version')

# Returns 409 and writes nothing if another client changed the session first.
# Re-read config_version and retry.
curl -X PATCH https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/tool_router/session/$SESSION_ID \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"toolkits": {"enable": ["gmail", "github"]}, "expected_config_version": '"$CONFIG_VERSION"'}'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

You can also pass a version you read elsewhere, for example one stored with a queued job. `expectedConfigVersion: false` (`expected_config_version=False`) is the same as omitting it. The API still commits only a fully validated configuration, so a losing update never leaves a half-applied session behind.

Raw HTTP callers set `expected_config_version` in the `PATCH` body themselves; without it the last writer wins.

To roll a session back, read a previous configuration from its config history (`GET /api/v3.1/tool_router/session/{session_id}/config_history`) and convert it into an update request. A history entry is not a request body: it carries metadata and version fields, and it names toolkits and tools as `enabled` and `disabled`, which map to `enable` and `disable` in the update.

### executeMeta() / execute_meta()

Run a `COMPOSIO_*` [meta tool](/toolkits/meta-tools) directly from your session with a slug and optional arguments:

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript', 'API']} persist>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
from composio import Composio

composio = Composio(api_key="your_api_key")
session = composio.create(user_id="user_123")
result = session.execute_meta(
    "COMPOSIO_SEARCH_TOOLS",
    arguments={"queries": [{"use_case": "send an email"}]},
)
print(result.data, result.result_type)
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
import { Composio } from '@composio/core';
const composio = new Composio({ apiKey: 'your_api_key' });
const session = await composio.create("user_123");
// ---cut---
const result = await session.executeMeta("COMPOSIO_SEARCH_TOOLS", {
  queries: [{ use_case: "send an email" }],
});
console.log(result.data, result.resultType);
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="API">
```bash
SESSION_ID=$(curl -s -X POST https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/tool_router/session \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"user_id": "user_123"}' | jq -r '.session_id')

curl -X POST https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/tool_router/session/$SESSION_ID/execute_meta \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"slug": "COMPOSIO_SEARCH_TOOLS", "arguments": {"queries": [{"use_case": "send an email"}]}}'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

The exported `ToolRouterSessionMetaToolSlug` type lists the accepted slugs. The response includes `resultType` (`result_type` in Python). If execution needs input, such as approval, the SDK raises `ComposioToolInputRequiredError` (`ToolInputRequiredError` in Python). Calls are sent once without retries, so retry only when the operation is safe to repeat.

In TypeScript, the third argument holds input-response options: `session.executeMeta(slug, args, { inputResponses, requestState })`. Request options belong in the fourth argument. To pass only request options, use `session.executeMeta(slug, args, undefined, requestOptions)`.

`COMPOSIO_MULTI_EXECUTE_TOOL` calls through this method run on the backend. Local tools named in those calls are not executed in your process.

```python
all_toolkits = []
cursor = None

while True:
    result = session.toolkits(limit=20, next_cursor=cursor)
    all_toolkits.extend(result.items)
    cursor = result.next_cursor
    if not cursor:
        break
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
import { Composio } from '@composio/core';
const composio = new Composio({ apiKey: 'your_api_key' });
const session = await composio.create("user_123");
// ---cut---
const allToolkits: any[] = [];
let cursor: string | undefined;

do {
  const { items, cursor: nextCursor } = await session.toolkits({ limit: 20, cursor });
  allToolkits.push(...items);
  cursor = nextCursor;
} while (cursor);
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="API">
```bash
CURSOR=""
while true; do
  PAGE=$(curl -s -X GET "https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/tool_router/session/$SESSION_ID/toolkits?limit=20${CURSOR:+&cursor=$CURSOR}" \
    -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY")
  echo "$PAGE" | jq -c '.items[]'
  CURSOR=$(echo "$PAGE" | jq -r '.next_cursor // empty')
  [ -z "$CURSOR" ] && break
done
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

### Configuration history

Inspect the configurations a session has used with `session.list_config_history(limit=10)` in Python or `await session.listConfigHistory({ limit: 10 })` in TypeScript. Results are newest first, with the live configuration first. Each `session.update()` archives the previous configuration.

The response contains `items` with each version's `config` and an `is_current` (Python) or `isCurrent` (TypeScript) flag. Pass the response's `next_cursor` (Python) or `nextCursor` (TypeScript) as `cursor` to fetch another page; `limit` supports up to 100 items per page.

### delete()

Delete a session when you're done with it. Deleted sessions immediately stop being retrievable or executable, and the call returns the deleted `session_id`. Deleting a missing or already-deleted session surfaces the backend `404`.

<Callout type="info">
Requires `@composio/core` ≥ `0.13.1` (TypeScript) or `composio` ≥ `0.17.1` (Python).
</Callout>

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript', 'API']} persist>
<Tab value="Python">
```python

print(result["session_id"], result["deleted"])
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
import { Composio } from '@composio/core';

const session = await composio.create('user_123');
// ---cut---

```
</Tab>

<Callout type="info">
If you're building an agent, we recommend using [sessions](/docs/configuring-sessions) instead. See [Managing multiple connected accounts](/docs/authentication/managing-multiple-connected-accounts) for how sessions handle account selection automatically.
</Callout>

Connected accounts are authenticated connections between your users and toolkits. After users authenticate (see [Authenticating tools](/docs/tools-direct/authenticating-tools)), you can manage these accounts throughout their lifecycle.

Composio automatically handles token refresh and credential management. This guide covers manual operations: listing, retrieving, refreshing, enabling, disabling, and deleting accounts.

## List accounts

```python
    user_ids=[user_id]

    statuses=["ACTIVE"]
)
```
  </Tab>

### Get account credentials

Connected-account responses describe the authentication state. Sensitive credential fields in `account.state.val` are [redacted by default](#credential-masking), for both Composio-managed and custom auth configs. This object is not a source of usable provider tokens for your own tools.

To call a provider API, use [Proxy Execute](/docs/extending-sessions/proxy-execute), which injects credentials server-side. For custom business logic, use [session extension tools](/docs/extending-sessions/local-tools-and-toolkits). See [Token custody architecture](/docs/security/token-custody) for the boundaries between your application, Composio, and the provider.

## Refresh credentials

<Callout type="warn">
`composio.connected_accounts.refresh()` in Python and `composio.connectedAccounts.refresh()` in TypeScript are deprecated. Re-initiate authentication with `link()` or `composio.toolkits.authorize()` instead. The refresh endpoint no longer validates credentials. TypeScript ignores `validateCredentials` and logs a warning when you set it.
</Callout>

Manually refresh credentials for a connected account:

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript', 'API']} persist>
  <Tab value="Python">
```python
try:
    refreshed = composio.connected_accounts.refresh(connected_account_id)
    print(f"Redirect URL: {refreshed.redirect_url}")

    # Wait for the connection to be established
    composio.connected_accounts.wait_for_connection(refreshed.id)
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Failed to refresh tokens: {e}")
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
import { Composio } from '@composio/core';
const composio = new Composio({ apiKey: 'your_api_key' });
const connectedAccountId = 'ca_123';
// ---cut---
try {
  const refreshed = await composio.connectedAccounts.refresh(connectedAccountId);
  console.log('Redirect URL:', refreshed.redirect_url);

  // Wait for the connection to be established
  await composio.connectedAccounts.waitForConnection(refreshed.id);
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Failed to refresh tokens:', error);
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="API">
```bash
# Deprecated endpoint: returns a redirect URL for re-authentication
curl -X POST https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/connected_accounts/ca_123/refresh \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" | jq -r '.redirect_url'

# Check whether the connection is ACTIVE again
curl -X GET https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/connected_accounts/ca_123 \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" | jq -r '.status'
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Enable and disable accounts

Change account status without deleting. Set to INACTIVE to pause access, or ACTIVE to restore. Useful for:
- Pausing access during subscription lapses
- Temporary disconnection

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript', 'API']} persist>
  <Tab value="Python">
```python
# Disable an account
disabled = composio.connected_accounts.disable(connected_account_id)
print(f"Account disabled status: {disabled.success}")

# Re-enable when needed
enabled = composio.connected_accounts.enable(connected_account_id)
print(f"Account enabled status: {enabled.success}")
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
import { Composio } from '@composio/core';
const composio = new Composio({ apiKey: 'your_api_key' });
const connectedAccountId = 'ca_123';
// ---cut---
// Disable an account
const disabled = await composio.connectedAccounts.disable(connectedAccountId);
console.log('Account disabled status:', disabled.success);

// Re-enable when needed
const enabled = await composio.connectedAccounts.enable(connectedAccountId);
console.log('Account enabled status:', enabled.success);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="API">
```bash
# Disable an account
curl -X PATCH https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/connected_accounts/ca_123/status \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"enabled": false}'

# Re-enable when needed
curl -X PATCH https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/connected_accounts/ca_123/status \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"enabled": true}'
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

<Callout type="warn">
INACTIVE accounts cannot execute tools. Tool execution will fail until the status is changed.
</Callout>

## Revoke accounts

To revoke upstream tokens and mark a connection `REVOKED`, call `composio.connected_accounts.revoke(connected_account_id)` in Python or `await composio.connectedAccounts.revoke(connectedAccountId)` in TypeScript. Upstream token revocation is best effort. The call fails if the toolkit does not support programmatic revocation or the account is not in a revokable state.

## Complete deferred OAuth

If your project has an OAuth callback verifier configured, Composio redirects to your verifier with a single-use session URI before activating the connection. Verify the person's identity in your application, then redeem the URI with `composio.connected_accounts.complete_auth(user_id=user_id, session_uri=session_uri)` in Python or `await composio.connectedAccounts.completeAuth({ userId, sessionUri })` in TypeScript.

Composio checks project ownership and the connection's user ID before completing the token exchange. An expired or already redeemed URI returns a `404`.

## Delete accounts

Permanently remove a connected account:

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript', 'API']} persist>
  <Tab value="Python">
```python
# Delete a connected account
composio.connected_accounts.delete(connected_account_id)
print("Account deleted successfully")
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
import { Composio } from '@composio/core';
const composio = new Composio({ apiKey: 'your_api_key' });
const connectedAccountId = 'ca_123';
// ---cut---
// Delete a connected account
await composio.connectedAccounts.delete(connectedAccountId);
console.log('Account deleted successfully');
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="API">
```bash
curl -X DELETE https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/connected_accounts/ca_123 \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY"
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

<Callout type="warn">
Deletion is permanent and cannot be undone.
</Callout>

## Credential masking

By default, sensitive fields in connected account responses are partially masked for security. This affects fields like `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `api_key`, `bearer_token`, `password`, and other secrets.

Instead of returning full values, the API returns the first 4 characters followed by `...`:

```json
{
  "access_token": "gho_...",
  "refresh_token": "ghr_...",
  "api_key": "sk-l..."
}
```

Values shorter than 4 characters are replaced with `REDACTED`.

This applies to the Get Connected Account and List Connected Accounts endpoints for both Composio-managed and custom auth configs. The API redacts these fields before returning the response to your application.

If your use case requires calling a provider API directly, use [Proxy execute](/docs/extending-sessions/proxy-execute). Composio injects the connected account's credentials server-side.

## Multiple accounts

Users can connect multiple accounts for the same toolkit (e.g., personal and work Gmail).

<Callout type="warn">
**For Composio-managed OAuth, prefer `link()`.** The `initiate()` examples below will stop working for Composio-managed OAuth auth configs starting **2026-05-08** (new orgs) / **2026-07-03** (all orgs). `link()` provides hosted authentication and is unaffected by the rollout. Like `initiate()`, it refuses to create a second active connection for the same user and auth config unless you pass `allow_multiple=True` (Python) or `allowMultiple: true` (TypeScript). See [Connect Link authentication](/docs/tools-direct/authenticating-tools#hosted-authentication-connect-link), the [migration guide](/docs/auth-configuration/migrating-initiate-to-link), or the [changelog entry](/docs/changelog/2026/04/24).

The `initiate()` examples remain accurate for **custom auth configs** (your own OAuth app) and **non-OAuth schemes** (API key, bearer, basic) — those are unaffected.
</Callout>

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript', 'API']} persist>
  <Tab value="Python">
```python
# First account
try:
    first_account = composio.connected_accounts.initiate(
        user_id=user_id,
        auth_config_id=auth_config_id
    )
    print(f"First account redirect URL: {first_account.redirect_url}")
    connected_first_account = first_account.wait_for_connection()
    print(f"First account status: {connected_first_account.status}")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error initiating first account: {e}")

# Second account - must explicitly allow multiple
try:
    second_account = composio.connected_accounts.initiate(
        user_id=user_id,
        auth_config_id=auth_config_id,
        allow_multiple=True  # Required for additional accounts
    )
    print(f"Second account redirect URL: {second_account.redirect_url}")
    connected_second_account = second_account.wait_for_connection()
    print(f"Second account status: {connected_second_account.status}")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error initiating second account: {e}")
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
import { Composio } from '@composio/core';
const composio = new Composio({ apiKey: 'your_api_key' });
const userId = 'user_123';
const authConfigId = 'ac_123';
// ---cut---
// First account
try {
  const firstAccount = await composio.connectedAccounts.initiate(
    userId,
    authConfigId
  );
  console.log('First account redirect URL:', firstAccount.redirectUrl);
  const connectedFirstAccount = await firstAccount.waitForConnection();
  console.log('First account status:', connectedFirstAccount.status);
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Error initiating first account:', error);
}

// Second account - must explicitly allow multiple
try {
  const secondAccount = await composio.connectedAccounts.initiate(
    userId,
    authConfigId,
    {
      allowMultiple: true  // Required for additional accounts
    }
  );
  console.log('Second account redirect URL:', secondAccount.redirectUrl);
  const connectedSecondAccount = await secondAccount.waitForConnection();
  console.log('Second account status:', connectedSecondAccount.status);
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Error initiating second account:', error);
}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="API">
```bash
# Each call creates a new connection for the same user and auth config.
# The API does not block duplicates; allow_multiple is an SDK-side check.
curl -X POST https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/connected_accounts \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"auth_config": {"id": "ac_123"}, "connection": {"user_id": "user_123"}}' | jq -r '.redirect_url'
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

<Callout type="info">
For session-based apps, see [Managing multiple connected accounts](/docs/authentication/managing-multiple-connected-accounts) for how to pass a specific account to a session.
</Callout>

### Execute with a specific account

When you have multiple accounts, specify which one to use with `connected_account_id`:

```python
    "GMAIL_GET_PROFILE",
    user_id=user_id,
    connected_account_id=connected_account_id,  # Specify which account to use
    version="20251111_00",
    arguments={}
)
print(f"Tool executed: {result}")
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
import { Composio } from '@composio/core';
const composio = new Composio({ apiKey: 'your_api_key' });

// Execute tool with a specific connected account

  userId: userId,
  connectedAccountId: connectedAccountId,  // Specify which account to use
  version: '20251111_00',
  arguments: {}

console.log('Tool executed:', result);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="API">
```bash

  -d '{"user_id": "user_123", "connected_account_id": "ca_123", "version": "20251111_00", "arguments": {}}'
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

REPOSITORY: ComposioHQ/composio
COMMIT: e7c4aac1e3b1fd05019d17a6e1010891c0917e6e

---
title: Managing multiple connected accounts
description: Handle users with multiple accounts for the same toolkit using multi-account mode and aliases
keywords: [multiple accounts, multi-account, work personal, switch account, alias, account selection]
---

Users can connect multiple accounts for the same toolkit (e.g., personal and work Gmail accounts). This guide covers how to enable multi-account mode, label accounts with aliases, and select which account to use.

## Multi-account mode

For a runnable agent with work and personal Gmail accounts, follow the [multiple accounts walkthrough](/examples/multiple-accounts).

By default, each session uses **one account per toolkit**. Enable multi-account mode to let users connect and use multiple accounts for the same toolkit within a single session.

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript', 'API']} persist>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
session = composio.create(
    user_id="user_123",
    toolkits=["gmail"],
    multi_account={
        "enable": True,
        "max_accounts_per_toolkit": 3,
    },
)
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
// @noErrors
import { Composio } from '@composio/core';
const composio = new Composio({ apiKey: 'your_api_key' });
// ---cut---
const session = await composio.create("user_123", {
  toolkits: ["gmail"],
  multiAccount: {
    enable: true,
    maxAccountsPerToolkit: 3,
  },
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="API">
```bash
# The SDKs default require_explicit_selection to true when multi-account mode is enabled
curl -X POST https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/tool_router/session \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "user_id": "user_123",
    "toolkits": {"enable": ["gmail"]},
    "multi_account": {"enable": true, "max_accounts_per_toolkit": 3, "require_explicit_selection": true}
  }'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

### Configuration options

| Option (TS / Python) | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| `enable` | `boolean` | `false` | Enable multi-account mode for this session |
| `maxAccountsPerToolkit` / `max_accounts_per_toolkit` | `number` | `5` | Maximum connected accounts per toolkit (2-10) |
| `requireExplicitSelection` / `require_explicit_selection` | `boolean` | `false` | When true and a toolkit has multiple active connected accounts, the agent must provide the `account` parameter in the tool execution call to select which account to use. `account` can be either a connected account ID or an alias (see the Aliases section below). When false, the default account (most recently connected active account) is used automatically |

When multi-account mode is disabled (the default), each session uses the most recently connected account for each toolkit.

## Connecting multiple accounts

Call `session.authorize()` multiple times for the same toolkit. Each call creates a separate connected account.

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript', 'API']} persist>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
session = composio.create(
    user_id="user_123",
    toolkits=["gmail"],
    multi_account={"enable": True},
)

# Connect work account
work_auth = session.authorize("gmail", alias="work-gmail")
print(f"Connect work Gmail: {work_auth.redirect_url}")
work_connection = work_auth.wait_for_connection()

# Connect personal account
personal_auth = session.authorize("gmail", alias="personal-gmail")
print(f"Connect personal Gmail: {personal_auth.redirect_url}")
personal_connection = personal_auth.wait_for_connection()
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
// @noErrors
import { Composio } from '@composio/core';
const composio = new Composio({ apiKey: 'your_api_key' });
// ---cut---
const session = await composio.create("user_123", {
  toolkits: ["gmail"],
  multiAccount: { enable: true },
});

// Connect work account
const workAuth = await session.authorize("gmail", { alias: "work-gmail" });
console.log(`Connect work Gmail: ${workAuth.redirectUrl}`);
const workConnection = await workAuth.waitForConnection();

// Connect personal account
const personalAuth = await session.authorize("gmail", { alias: "personal-gmail" });
console.log(`Connect personal Gmail: ${personalAuth.redirectUrl}`);
const personalConnection = await personalAuth.waitForConnection();
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="API">
```bash
SESSION_ID=$(curl -s -X POST https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/tool_router/session \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "user_id": "user_123",
    "toolkits": {"enable": ["gmail"]},
    "multi_account": {"enable": true, "require_explicit_selection": true}
  }' | jq -r '.session_id')

# Connect work account
curl -s -X POST https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/tool_router/session/$SESSION_ID/link \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"toolkit": "gmail", "alias": "work-gmail"}' | jq -r '.redirect_url'

# Connect personal account
curl -s -X POST https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/tool_router/session/$SESSION_ID/link \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"toolkit": "gmail", "alias": "personal-gmail"}' | jq -r '.redirect_url'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Aliases

Aliases are human-readable labels for connected accounts (e.g., `"work-gmail"`, `"personal-github"`). They make it easier for agents and users to identify which account is which.

- Must be unique per user and toolkit within a project
- Can be set during connection or updated after

To identify an account by its provider-side identity (e.g. the Gmail address or GitHub username) rather than a label you set, read the read-only `displayName` that Composio auto-populates on the connected account at `state.val.displayName` once the connection is active.

See [Identify the connected account](/docs/authentication/manually-authenticating#identify-the-connected-account) to display that identity or retrieve the provider's profile. To accept only certain email domains, follow [Restrict Gmail connections to an email domain](/examples/restrict-gmail-domain).

### Setting an alias during connection

Pass `alias` to `session.authorize()`:

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript', 'API']} persist>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
session = composio.create(user_id="user_123")

connection_request = session.authorize("gmail", alias="work-gmail")
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
// @noErrors
import { Composio } from '@composio/core';
const composio = new Composio({ apiKey: 'your_api_key' });
const session = await composio.create("user_123");
// ---cut---
const connectionRequest = await session.authorize("gmail", { alias: "work-gmail" });
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="API">
```bash
SESSION_ID=$(curl -s -X POST https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/tool_router/session \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"user_id": "user_123"}' | jq -r '.session_id')

curl -X POST https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/tool_router/session/$SESSION_ID/link \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"toolkit": "gmail", "alias": "work-gmail"}'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

The direct-execution methods `connectedAccounts.initiate()` and `connectedAccounts.link()` accept the same `alias` parameter. To create another active connection for the same user and auth config, also pass `allow_multiple=True` in Python or `allowMultiple: true` in TypeScript.

### Updating or clearing an alias

```bash
  -d '{"alias": "work-gmail"}'

# Clear an alias
curl -X PATCH https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/connected_accounts/ca_abc123 \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"alias": ""}'
```
</Tab>

```python
for toolkit in toolkits.items:
```

===== BEGIN FILE: composio/إدارة-الجلسات-والأدوات/migration-guide-toolkit-versioning.mdx =====
REPOSITORY: ComposioHQ/composio
COMMIT: e7c4aac1e3b1fd05019d17a6e1010891c0917e6e
LICENSE: MIT / ISC(TS) / Apache-2.0(Python)

---
title: Toolkit versioning migration
description: Migrate to the new toolkit versioning system
written: "October 2025"
---

Starting with Python SDK v0.9.0 and TypeScript SDK v0.2.0, manual tool execution requires explicit version specification. This is a breaking change from earlier versions where toolkit versioning was optional.

## Breaking change

Manual tool execution now requires explicit version specification. The `tools.execute()` method will fail without a version.

### Before (will fail)

{/* code-example: no-api reason="ToolVersionRequiredError is raised client-side by the SDK version check" */}
<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript']} persist>
  <Tab value="Python">
```python
# Raises ToolVersionRequiredError
result = composio.tools.execute(
    "GITHUB_CREATE_ISSUE",
    arguments={"owner": "composio", "repo": "composio", "title": "Bug report"},
    user_id="user-123",
)
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
// @noErrors
// Throws ComposioToolVersionRequiredError
const result = await composio.tools.execute("GITHUB_CREATE_ISSUE", {
    userId: "user-123",
    arguments: { owner: "composio", repo: "composio", title: "Bug report" }
});
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

### After (required)

Choose one of three migration strategies:

#### Option 1: Configure version at SDK level

{/* code-example: no-api reason="toolkit_versions is an SDK constructor option; the REST API takes version per request" */}
<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript']} persist>
  <Tab value="Python">
```python
from composio import Composio

# Pin specific versions for each toolkit
composio = Composio(
    api_key="YOUR_API_KEY",
    toolkit_versions={
        "github": "20251027_00",
        "slack": "20251027_00",
        "gmail": "20251027_00"
    }
)
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
// @noErrors
import { Composio } from "@composio/core";

// Pin specific versions for each toolkit
const composio = new Composio({
    apiKey: "YOUR_API_KEY",
    toolkitVersions: {
        github: "20251027_00",
        slack: "20251027_00",
        gmail: "20251027_00"
    }
});
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

#### Option 2: Pass version with each execution

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript', 'API']} persist>
  <Tab value="Python">
```python
# Specify version directly in execute call
result = composio.tools.execute(
    "GITHUB_LIST_STARGAZERS",
    arguments={
        "owner": "ComposioHQ",
        "repo": "composio"
    },
    user_id="user-k7334",
    version="20251027_00"  # Override version for this execution
)
print(result)
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
// @noErrors
// Specify version directly in execute call
const result = await composio.tools.execute("GITHUB_LIST_STARGAZERS", {
    userId: "user-k7334",
    arguments: {
        owner: "ComposioHQ",
        repo: "composio"
    },
    version: "20251027_00"  // Override version for this execution
});
console.log(result);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="API">
```bash
curl -X POST https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/tools/execute/GITHUB_LIST_STARGAZERS \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "user_id": "user-k7334",
    "arguments": {"owner": "ComposioHQ", "repo": "composio"},
    "version": "20251027_00"
  }'
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

#### Option 3: Use environment variables

```bash
export COMPOSIO_TOOLKIT_VERSION_GITHUB="20251027_00"
```

## Migration checklist

1. **Audit your code**: Find all `tools.execute()` calls in your codebase
2. **Choose a strategy**: Select one of the three options above based on your needs
3. **Test thoroughly**: Verify tools work correctly with pinned versions
4. **Deploy gradually**: Roll out changes incrementally to minimize risk

## Temporary workaround

During migration, you can temporarily skip version checks (not recommended for production):

{/* code-example: no-api reason="dangerously_skip_version_check only bypasses the SDK's client-side version check" */}
<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript']} persist>
  <Tab value="Python">
```python
result = composio.tools.execute(
    "GITHUB_CREATE_ISSUE",
    arguments={"owner": "composio", "repo": "composio", "title": "Bug report"},
    user_id="user-123",
    dangerously_skip_version_check=True,
)
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
// @noErrors
const result = await composio.tools.execute("GITHUB_CREATE_ISSUE", {
    userId: "user-123",
    arguments: { owner: "composio", repo: "composio", title: "Bug report" },
    dangerouslySkipVersionCheck: true
});
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

<Callout type="warn">
The `dangerouslySkipVersionCheck` flag is only for migration or debugging. Never use in production.
</Callout>

===== BEGIN FILE: composio/إدارة-الجلسات-والأدوات/sessions-via-mcp.mdx =====
REPOSITORY: ComposioHQ/composio
COMMIT: e7c4aac1e3b1fd05019d17a6e1010891c0917e6e
LICENSE: MIT / ISC(TS) / Apache-2.0(Python)
SHA256: 556bc129e34d4bbb4708d9967b79ba99669e78d901d7abc6beba267da638f59b

---
title: Using sessions via MCP
description: Build an application that exposes a Composio session to an MCP-compatible client
keywords: [mcp, model context protocol, sessions, remote server, hosted mcp]
---

Use this guide when you are building an application with Composio and want to expose one user's session over MCP. The application creates and configures the session, then passes its hosted MCP endpoint to a compatible client.

By default, Composio gives your agent tools it can call directly through a [provider package](/docs/providers). That is what the [Quickstart](/docs/quickstart) uses. Set `mcp: true` when an MCP transport fits your application better. No provider package is required for this route.

<Callout type="info" title="Connecting an existing agent instead?">
If you use Codex or Claude Code and did not explicitly choose MCP, install the native [Composio agent plugin](/docs/agent-plugins). If you explicitly want MCP in an existing client, use [Composio Connect](/docs/composio-connect).
</Callout>

<Callout type="info">
Want to bring tools from your own remote MCP server into Composio instead? See [Custom MCP](/docs/extending-sessions/custom-mcp).
</Callout>

## The MCP endpoint

If you use a scoped project API key, enable **Session management** to create and configure sessions and **Session tool execution** for session-linked MCP access. See [API key permissions](/reference/authenticating-to-composio/project-api-key-permissions) for access levels and routes.

Opt into MCP by passing `mcp: true` when you create the session. The session then exposes its hosted MCP server. Read the URL and headers off `session.mcp`:

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript', 'API']} persist>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
from composio import Composio

composio = Composio()
session = composio.sessions.create(user_id="user_123", mcp=True)

mcp_url = session.mcp.url
mcp_headers = session.mcp.headers
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
import { Composio } from "@composio/core";

const composio = new Composio();
const session = await composio.create("user_123", { mcp: true });

const mcpUrl = session.mcp.url;
const mcpHeaders = session.mcp.headers;
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="API">
```bash
# The MCP server accepts the same x-api-key header
curl -s -X POST https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/tool_router/session \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"user_id": "user_123"}' | jq -r '.mcp.url'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

You don't need a provider package to use the MCP endpoint, so you can drop it from your `Composio()` setup if MCP is all you need.

<Callout type="info">
Resuming a stored session? Pass the same flag, `composio.use(sessionId, { mcp: true })` (TypeScript) or `composio.use(session_id, mcp=True)` (Python), to surface `session.mcp` on the reused session.
</Callout>

<Callout type="info">
The MCP endpoint and `session.tools()` are backed by the same session. Toolkits, auth configs, and connected accounts you set when [configuring the session](/docs/configuring-sessions) apply to both.
</Callout>

## Approval without elicitation support

You can [require approval for session tools](/docs/configuring-sessions#requiring-tool-approval). If your MCP client cannot ask for approval through elicitation, set `experimental.noElicitationSupportFallback` in TypeScript or `experimental.no_elicitation_support_fallback` in Python when creating the session:

- `"deny"` blocks the call when the client cannot ask for approval.
- `"allow"` lets the call run without asking for approval.

For example, pass `experimental: { noElicitationSupportFallback: "deny" }` in TypeScript or `experimental={"no_elicitation_support_fallback": "deny"}` in Python alongside `mcp: true` or `mcp=True`.

## What the MCP headers carry

`session.mcp.headers` holds the credential the SDK used to create or load the session, and nothing else. No other default header and no ambient `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` is copied in.

| SDK credential | Exported header | What it can reach |
|---|---|---|
| Project API key (`apiKey`, `COMPOSIO_API_KEY`, or the project key stored by `composio login`) | `x-api-key` | That one project |
| User API key only (`apiKey: null` with `userApiKey` in TypeScript, `disable_api_key=True` with `user_api_key` in Python, or an `x-user-api-key` default header) | `x-user-api-key` | Every project the user can reach across your organization |

Treat the exported config as a secret and store it where you keep the project API key. A user-only session exports the user's organization-wide key, which makes it the broader credential: prefer a project-key session when an MCP client only needs one project. The SDK also exports `x-org-id` and `x-project-id` when the instance is scoped to a consumer project (see [Run sessions in your organization's consumer project](/docs/consumer-agents#run-sessions-in-your-organizations-consumer-project)).

The SDK attaches the headers only when the MCP URL has the same origin as the API base URL it talks to, whatever the scheme, so a custom `baseURL` works as long as it serves the session MCP endpoint. For any other destination, `create()` and `use()` called with `mcp: true` (TypeScript) or `mcp=True` (Python) raise `ComposioMCPDestinationError` or `MCPDestinationError`; the error names both origins and never the key. Without the MCP flag the session is still returned, `session.mcp.headers` is empty, and the SDK logs a warning naming both origins, so agents that only use native tools keep working. The SDK never connects to the MCP URL itself and never follows redirects for it. Configure your MCP client so it does not forward these headers to a different origin either.

<Callout type="info">
Requires `@composio/core` ≥ `0.19.1` (TypeScript) or `composio` ≥ `0.22.1` (Python). Earlier releases only exported a project key, so a session driven with a user API key had no usable MCP headers. Pass `session.mcp.headers` through as returned instead of assembling an `x-api-key` header from an environment variable yourself.
</Callout>

## A single URL for a fixed set of tools

Combine `mcp: true` with the [direct-tools preset](/docs/configuring-sessions) to get one MCP URL that serves exactly the tools you list, with no search or meta tools in front of them. This is the closest equivalent to a classic hosted MCP server scoped to a handful of tools.

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript', 'API']} persist>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
from composio import Composio, SESSION_PRESET_DIRECT_TOOLS

composio = Composio()

session = composio.sessions.create(
    user_id="user_123",
    toolkits=["gmail"],
    tools={"gmail": {"enable": ["GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS", "GMAIL_CREATE_EMAIL_DRAFT"]}},
    session_preset=SESSION_PRESET_DIRECT_TOOLS,
    mcp=True,
)

# A single MCP URL that exposes just these two tools
print(session.mcp.url)
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
import { Composio, SessionPreset } from "@composio/core";

const composio = new Composio();

const session = await composio.create("user_123", {
  toolkits: ["gmail"],
  tools: { gmail: { enable: ["GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS", "GMAIL_CREATE_EMAIL_DRAFT"] } },
  sessionPreset: SessionPreset.DIRECT_TOOLS,
  mcp: true,
});

// A single MCP URL that exposes just these two tools
console.log(session.mcp.url);
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="API">
```bash
# The SDK's direct-tools preset sends the last five fields; prints a single MCP URL for just these two tools
curl -s -X POST https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/tool_router/session \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "user_id": "user_123",
    "toolkits": {"enable": ["gmail"]},
    "tools": {"gmail": {"enable": ["GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS", "GMAIL_CREATE_EMAIL_DRAFT"]}},
    "manage_connections": {"enable": false},
    "workbench": {"enable": false},
    "preload": {"tools": "all"},
    "search": {"enable": false},
    "execute": {"enable_multi_execute": false}
  }' | jq -r '.mcp.url'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Any MCP client pointed at that URL sees only `GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS` and `GMAIL_CREATE_EMAIL_DRAFT`. See [Configuring Sessions](/docs/configuring-sessions) for the full set of toolkit, tool, and auth filters.

## Wire it into your framework

Pass `session.mcp.url` and `session.mcp.headers` to your framework's MCP client.

For complete CrewAI and LangChain scripts, follow the [Python MCP research agent example](/examples/python-mcp-agents).

```python
    ],

```

## Trade-offs

MCP is the more portable option. Any MCP-compatible client connects with just a URL, and it's supported across more frameworks and apps (Claude Desktop, Cursor, the OpenAI Responses API, and others) without a provider package.

The trade-off is that the MCP client talks to Composio's server directly, so anything the SDK does *around* tool execution doesn't apply:

- **Tool-call modifiers don't run.** `beforeExecute` / `afterExecute` hooks and `modifySchema` transforms live in the SDK's execution path. Over MCP the client executes tools against the server and bypasses them, so you can't intercept, reshape, log, or gate calls the way you can with tools your agent calls directly.
- **Session-bound custom tools and toolkits don't work.** Tools created with `experimental_createTool` / `experimental_createToolkit` in TypeScript, or `composio.experimental.tool` / `composio.experimental.Toolkit` in Python, run in your process. The MCP server only exposes Composio's hosted tools, so your local custom tools aren't available over the endpoint.

If you need any of those, call tools directly through a [provider](/docs/providers) instead of over MCP.

===== BEGIN FILE: composio/إدارة-الجلسات-والأدوات/tool-hints.mdx =====
REPOSITORY: ComposioHQ/composio
COMMIT: e7c4aac1e3b1fd05019d17a6e1010891c0917e6e
LICENSE: MIT / ISC(TS) / Apache-2.0(Python)
SHA256: f7f890c6b6490af474b2ead731487300b777cb75b32e73889b2ee51e3a7c7819

---
title: Tool hints
description: How Composio classifies each tool by the action it takes, and how sessions use those hints
keywords: [tags, readOnlyHint, createHint, updateHint, destructiveHint, governance, permissions]
---

Every tool has a **hint** that describes the action it takes: reading, creating, updating or deleting. In [sessions](/docs/configuring-sessions), you can use these hints to configure the tools available in the session.

<span id="tags" className="block scroll-m-28" />

## Hints

| Hint | The tool | For example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `readOnlyHint` | Reads data without changing anything. This includes tools that search, list, compute or export data. | Fetch emails, list pull requests, export a report |
| `createHint` | Adds something new, such as a message, record or file. It doesn't change anything that already exists. | Send an email, create an issue |
| `updateHint` | Changes something that already exists, such as its content or settings. It doesn't delete anything. | Edit an issue, rename a file |
| `destructiveHint` | Deletes something, such as a file, record or repository. A tool that can delete something has this hint, even if it also creates or updates. | Delete a file, delete a repository |

<span id="how-tools-are-tagged" className="block scroll-m-28" />

## How tools get hints

Composio assigns hints on a best-effort basis, based on each tool's description and behavior. For MCP tools, Composio infers them from the tool's description and the hints the MCP server provides.

<span id="using-tags-in-a-session" className="block scroll-m-28" />

## Using hints in a session

A session can allow, block or require approval for tools by their hint, and override this for specific toolkits:

- To block tools, see [Filtering tools by tags](/docs/configuring-sessions#filtering-tools-by-tags).
- To require approval, see [Approvals](/docs/governance/approvals).

  icon={<Wrench />}
  title="Approvals"
  href="/docs/governance/approvals"
  description="Require the user's approval before tools run."

REPOSITORY: ComposioHQ/composio
COMMIT: e7c4aac1e3b1fd05019d17a6e1010891c0917e6e
LICENSE: MIT / ISC(TS) / Apache-2.0(Python)
SHA256: 12e48c13ac59d72029615bceae4cef4d53c1dd7ff1be3bbb5a553b3702c07bd4

---
title: Toolkit Versioning
description: Pin a tool version per execute call or configure defaults for consistent behavior in production
keywords: [version, pin version, tool versioning, tools.execute, per-execution override]
llmGuardrails: "direct-execution"
legacy: true
---

<Callout type="info">
If you're building an agent, we recommend using [sessions](/docs/configuring-sessions) instead. Sessions handle toolkit versions automatically so you don't have to manage them yourself.
</Callout>

Toolkit versioning ensures your tools behave consistently across deployments. You can pin specific versions in production, test new releases in development, and roll back when needed.

## Per-execution override

Pass `version` directly to `composio.tools.execute()` to pin one call. The per-call value takes precedence over SDK initialization and environment variables, and leaves the defaults for other calls unchanged.

These examples use `20251027_00`. Replace it with an available version you have tested for your toolkit.

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript', 'API']} persist>
  <Tab value="Python">
```python
from composio import Composio

composio = Composio(api_key="YOUR_API_KEY")

result = composio.tools.execute(
    "GITHUB_LIST_STARGAZERS",
    arguments={
        "owner": "ComposioHQ",
        "repo": "composio"
    },
    user_id="user-k7334",
    version="20251027_00",
)
print(result)
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
import { Composio } from "@composio/core";

const composio = new Composio({ apiKey: "YOUR_API_KEY" });

const result = await composio.tools.execute("GITHUB_LIST_STARGAZERS", {
    userId: "user-k7334",
    version: "20251027_00",
    arguments: {
        owner: "ComposioHQ",
        repo: "composio"
    }
});
console.log(result);
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="API">
```bash
curl -X POST https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3.1/tools/execute/GITHUB_LIST_STARGAZERS \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"user_id": "user-k7334", "version": "20251027_00", "arguments": {"owner": "ComposioHQ", "repo": "composio"}}'
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

A dated version passes the direct-execution version check without a bypass flag. See [Direct Tool Execution](/docs/tools-direct/executing-tools#direct-tool-execution) for more examples.

## Find available versions

To view recent versions, go to [Dashboard](https://dashboard.composio.dev?utm_source=docs&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=docs-tools-direct-toolkit-versioning) > **All Toolkits** > select a toolkit. Use the version dropdown to choose a version:

![Toolkit version selector on the Composio dashboard](/images/toolkit-version-dashboard.png)

You can also find the latest version for each toolkit on the [Toolkits](/toolkits) page in the docs. Select a toolkit to see its current version and available tools.

<Callout type="info">
The toolkit metadata's `available_versions` list (`availableVersions` in TypeScript) contains at most the 50 newest versions. A version dropping out of that list does not retire it or stop pinned execution. Use the [deprecation and sunset policy](#deprecation-and-sunset), response warnings, and execution errors to determine when you need to upgrade. Keep your tested version in your own configuration rather than replacing it just because it is absent from the discovery list.
</Callout>

<Callout type="info">
Starting from Python SDK v0.9.0 and TypeScript SDK v0.2.0, specifying versions is required for manual tool execution — and `"latest"` is **not** accepted there on its own. To run the newest version with `tools.execute()`, pass `dangerously_skip_version_check=True` (TypeScript: `dangerouslySkipVersionCheck: true`) on the call; otherwise pin a dated version. `"latest"` works without the flag everywhere else (fetching tools, sessions).
</Callout>

## Default version behavior

<Callout type="warn">
The v3 API defaults to the base version (`00000000_00`) when you don't specify a version. This can return fewer tools than the [platform UI](https://dashboard.composio.dev?utm_source=docs&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=docs-tools-direct-toolkit-versioning). Pass `toolkit_versions=latest` or a specific version to select a newer version. The v3.1 tools API defaults to the latest version.
</Callout>

For example, a v3 tools-list request without `toolkit_versions` returns the base version:

<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript', 'API']} persist>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
from composio import Composio

composio = Composio()
base_version = composio.client.get(
    "/api/v3/tools",
    cast_to=object,
    query={"toolkit_slug": "googledrive"},
)
latest_version = composio.client.get(
    "/api/v3/tools",
    cast_to=object,
    query={"toolkit_slug": "googledrive", "toolkit_versions": "latest"},
)
print(base_version, latest_version)
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
import { Composio } from '@composio/core';

const composio = new Composio();
const client = composio.getClient();
const baseVersion = await client.get<unknown>('/api/v3/tools', {
  query: { toolkit_slug: 'googledrive' },
});
const latestVersion = await client.get<unknown>('/api/v3/tools', {
  query: { toolkit_slug: 'googledrive', toolkit_versions: 'latest' },
});
console.log(baseVersion, latestVersion);
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="API">
{/* code-example: unchecked-api rule="api-legacy-version" operation="GET /api/v3/tools" reason="this example deliberately compares the previous REST version's default with an explicit latest version" */}
```bash
# Without toolkit_versions: returns tools from the base version
curl -X GET "https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/tools?toolkit_slug=googledrive" \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY"

# With toolkit_versions=latest: returns tools from the latest version
curl -X GET "https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/tools?toolkit_slug=googledrive&toolkit_versions=latest" \
  -H "x-api-key: $COMPOSIO_API_KEY"
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Configuration methods

To use the same version across calls, set a default at SDK initialization or through environment variables. A [per-execution override](#per-execution-override) takes precedence over either default.

### SDK initialization

{/* code-example: no-api reason="SDK constructor option sets client-side default toolkit versions" */}
<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript']} persist>
  <Tab value="Python">
```python
from composio import Composio

# Pin specific versions for each toolkit
composio = Composio(
    api_key="YOUR_API_KEY",
    toolkit_versions={
        "github": "20251027_00",
        "slack": "20251027_00",
        "gmail": "20251027_00"
    }
)
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
import { Composio } from "@composio/core";

// Pin specific versions for each toolkit
const composio = new Composio({
    apiKey: "YOUR_API_KEY",
    toolkitVersions: {
        github: "20251027_00",
        slack: "20251027_00",
        gmail: "20251027_00"
    }
});
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

### Environment variables

```bash
# Set versions for specific toolkits
export COMPOSIO_TOOLKIT_VERSION_GITHUB="20251027_00"
export COMPOSIO_TOOLKIT_VERSION_SLACK="20251027_00"
export COMPOSIO_TOOLKIT_VERSION_GMAIL="20251027_00"
```

## Version format

Versions follow the format `YYYYMMDD_NN`:
- `YYYYMMDD`: Release date
- `NN`: Sequential release number

{/* code-example: no-api reason="Shows SDK toolkit_versions value formats, not an HTTP call" */}
<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript']} persist>
  <Tab value="Python">
```python
# Pin to a specific version
toolkit_versions = {"github": "20251027_00"}

# Always use the newest tools (manual execution additionally requires
# dangerously_skip_version_check=True on the execute call)
toolkit_versions = {"github": "latest"}
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript
// Pin to a specific version
const pinned = { github: "20251027_00" };

// Always use the newest tools (manual execution additionally requires
// dangerouslySkipVersionCheck: true on the execute call)
const newest = { github: "latest" };
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Choosing between `latest` and a pinned version

The right choice depends on how your application consumes tool outputs:

- **Use `latest`** when tool outputs are consumed by an LLM or AI agent. Agents interpret responses dynamically and adapt to changes in output structure. Using `latest` ensures your agent always has access to the newest tools and improvements without manual intervention. For manual execution (`tools.execute()`), `latest` requires the explicit opt-in `dangerously_skip_version_check=True` / `dangerouslySkipVersionCheck: true` on the call — the flag's name is the reminder that output schemas can change between releases.

- **Pin a specific version** when tool outputs are consumed programmatically — for example, if your code destructures specific fields from a response, maps outputs to a database schema, or feeds results into a typed pipeline. Schema changes in a new version could silently break these integrations.

<Callout type="info">
As a rule of thumb: if an LLM reads the output, use `latest`. If your code parses the output, pin the version.
</Callout>

Most agentic applications — including all [session-based](/docs/configuring-sessions) workflows — use `latest` by default and benefit from always having the most up-to-date tools. If you're building structured data pipelines or integrations with fixed response parsing, pin to a tested version and upgrade on your own schedule.

## Version resolution order

1. Per-execution version (highest priority)
2. SDK initialization version
3. Environment variable (toolkit-specific)

## Managing versions

Check available versions using:

  <Tab value="Python">
```python
# Get toolkit information including available versions
toolkit = composio.toolkits.get(slug="github")

# Extract and print version information
print(f"Toolkit: {toolkit.name}")
print(f"Current Version: {toolkit.meta.version}")
print(f"Available Versions: {toolkit.meta.available_versions}")
```

```typescript
// Extract and print version information
```

### Retrieve toolkit changelogs

Call `composio.toolkits.changelog()` in Python or `await composio.toolkits.changelog()` in TypeScript to retrieve the last 10 versions for each toolkit. The response's `items` contain each toolkit's slug and version entries, which you can review before changing a pinned version.

## Deprecation and sunset

Composio-managed toolkit versions are deprecated 12 months after they're published and retired 3 months after that. The newest version of a toolkit is never deprecated, so pinning a current version and upgrading on your own schedule keeps you clear of both dates.

When a request resolves to a deprecated version, the API adds a `Composio-Deprecated-Toolkits` response header alongside the normal response:

```http
Composio-Deprecated-Toolkits: "GMAIL";version="20250114_00";deprecated=@1779840000;sunset=@1787788800;reason="lifecycle"
```

The header is an RFC 9651 structured-field list. Each item names the toolkit slug and the resolved `version`, plus optional `deprecated` and `sunset` dates (Unix seconds, prefixed with `@`) and a `reason`. Versions deprecated by hand carry only `version`.

Single-toolkit routes carry the header: toolkit get, tool get, tool execute, text-to-request, trigger type get, trigger upsert and setup, and trigger authorization entities. Listing endpoints never do.

### SDK warning

Both SDKs read the header and warn once per process for each deprecated toolkit version. The call still succeeds.

{/* code-example: no-api reason="SDK deprecation warning output and local warning/logger filtering" */}
<Tabs groupId="language" items={['Python', 'TypeScript']} persist>
  <Tab value="Python">
```text
[Deprecation] Toolkit GMAIL version 20250114_00 was deprecated on 2026-05-27 (lifecycle) and will stop working on 2026-08-27. Pin a newer version with toolkit_versions={"gmail": "<version>"} or COMPOSIO_TOOLKIT_VERSION_GMAIL. See https://docs.composio.dev/docs/tools-direct/toolkit-versioning#deprecation-and-sunset.
```

The warning is a `ComposioDeprecationWarning` (a `UserWarning` subclass), so standard warning filters apply:

```python
import warnings
from composio import ComposioDeprecationWarning

warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=ComposioDeprecationWarning)
```
  </Tab>
  <Tab value="TypeScript">
```text
[Deprecation] Toolkit GMAIL version 20250114_00 was deprecated on 2026-05-27 (lifecycle) and will stop working on 2026-08-27. Pin a newer version with toolkitVersions: { gmail: '<version>' } or COMPOSIO_TOOLKIT_VERSION_GMAIL. See https://docs.composio.dev/docs/tools-direct/toolkit-versioning#deprecation-and-sunset.
```

The warning goes through the SDK logger at the `warn` level. Silence it with `logLevel: 'error'` in the constructor or `COMPOSIO_LOG_LEVEL=error` in the environment:

```typescript
import { Composio } from '@composio/core';

const composio = new Composio({ logLevel: 'error' });
```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

When the header omits `reason` or `sunset`, the warning omits those clauses too.

### Moving off a deprecated version

Pick a newer version from the [dashboard](https://dashboard.composio.dev?utm_source=docs&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=docs-tools-direct-toolkit-versioning) or `toolkits.get()`, then pin it the same way you pin any version: at [SDK initialization](#sdk-initialization), through an [environment variable](#environment-variables), or [per execute call](#per-execution-override). The warning stops as soon as requests resolve to a version that isn't deprecated.

After the sunset date, requests for the retired version fail with HTTP `410 Gone` until you pin a supported version.

title: Toolkit Versioning
